per_window.ps-ns: dynamic_in_window in the acidic loop and the chain ends. The 2015 NMR study, now read in full, measures R1, R2 and NOE at 800 MHz and 30 °C on perdeuterated full-length UBE2G1 (0.8 mM, pH 7.0, 50 mM HEPES, 100 mM NaCl, 5 mM DTT) and finds the acidic loop 97-109 and the termini more flexible than the core, which tumbles with a correlation time of roughly 12-14 ns (UBE2G1-J3); no order parameters or internal correlation times were fitted and the values are figure-only.
per_window.us-ms: search_insufficient (UBE2G1-J4): the one relaxation study fits no exchange term and no dispersion, CEST or R1rho experiment exists. Its Figure 3 shows uncommented R2 outliers near residues 27 (about 37 s-1) and 126 (about 42 s-1, with 128-131 elevated) against a 20-25 s-1 baseline; a lead for a future dispersion measurement, not an exchange claim.
per_window.undetermined: UbV.G1.1-bound 6D68 superposes on apo 2AWF with backbone RMSD 0.66 A (UBE2G1-J2, r4, structure_only); the 2015 JBC abstract implicates the Y102-G103-Y104 acidic loop in binding donor ubiquitin in an oxyester conjugate (UBE2G1-J1, r1); the gaps in the 2015 assignment table are proline and glycine chemistry, not exchange (UBE2G1-J6). Not judged: r2 and r3 (two-state and one-state ubiquitin on the Ube2r1 paralog, abstract only); r5 to r8 (E1 charging and discharge gel assays of wild type and S26R with UbV.G1.1: product accumulation, not conformational motion).

protein_summary.wt_apo_answer: Unknown: the relaxation study of free full-length UBE2G1 (800 MHz, 30 °C, pH 7.0, HEPES/NaCl/DTT, 0.8 mM perdeuterated protein), now identified and read in full, reports R1, R2 and NOE and reads the acidic loop 97-109 and the termini as more flexible, but fits no exchange term and runs no dispersion experiment, so no us-ms exchange, rate or population is measured; the isolated R2 outliers near residues 27 and 126 in its Figure 3 are uncommented by the authors.
questions_for_gina: The 2015 assignment paper (doi:10.1186/s40543-015-0068-z) measures 800 MHz R1, R2 and NOE at 30 °C on full-length Ube2g1 and matches the entry's relaxation set; can it be confirmed as the RelaxDB source, since the card carries no BMRB id?

Its Figure 3 shows uncommented R2 values of about 37 s-1 near residue 27 and about 42 s-1 near residue 126 against a 20-25 s-1 baseline: should these be flagged as candidate exchange sites for a dispersion measurement, or does the RelaxDB label already use them?
protein_summary.buffer_note: The 2015 relaxation and assignment paper (doi:10.1186/s40543-015-0068-z) was read in full on 2026-10-20 (case S6_r6_UBE2G1_20261020224441); its protein is GST-cleaved M1-E170, the entry sequence plus two cloning residues G-2 and S-1, and it is treated here as the entry construct. Relaxation was recorded at 30 °C and 800 MHz, the assignments at 25 °C and 900 MHz; the two conditions are not conflated. All relaxation values are read from Figure 3, a plot. The protein runs at an apparent 25 kDa against a 20 kDa sequence mass, which the paper notes without a quantitative model or an independent test for oligomerisation. The 2015 JBC rows (r1-r3) are abstract-only and give no conditions. The 2020 rows (r4-r8) are full text: crystal at 20 °C, pH 8.0 in PEG1500/SPG; charging assays at 30 °C, pH 7.5, 20 mM HEPES, 100 mM NaCl, 5 mM MgCl2 with ATP; discharge adds apyrase, lysine and 25 mM EDTA. Construct boundaries differ: entry and 6D68 are full length (1-170), apo 2AWF and the assay protein are 8-160. Second read flagged r6 earlier; adjudication B confirmed that row, and both readers passed the two new rows with no flags.

detection.detection_window: Two static crystal structures, one bound to an engineered UbV and one apo, compared by global backbone RMSD (0.66 Å); this sees only a binding-induced change in the averaged crystal conformation and cannot see motion on any timescale, local loop changes hidden by the global RMSD, or solution exchange.

judgments.reason: Backside binding of UbV.G1.1 leaves the UBE2G1 backbone almost unchanged relative to apo 2AWF (RMSD 0.66 Å, 'virtually no differences'); a static cross-construct comparison, not evidence against motion. Two static structures (one bound) define no detection window, so this cannot count as 'not detected' (batch-3 review).

judgments.reason: Full text of the 2015 NMR study, now identified as the source of the entry's relaxation set: the acidic loop 97-109 and the chain ends show the relaxation signature of faster local backbone motion than the structured core, which tumbles with a correlation time of roughly 12-14 ns; no order parameter, internal correlation time or model-free fit is reported, and the per-residue values are a figure (sources_cache/10.1186_s40543-015-0068-z.pdf, Fig. 3 and caption p. 5, Results p. 6, Methods p. 4).
